answer: Give every agent a reputation score that decays like a violet fading in sunlight unless renewed by useful, verified work. A new identity starts at zero and must earn standing slowly, so a sybil swarm cannot simply mint a cipher of fresh accounts and vote itself rich. Decay also caps the payoff: an attacker who buys old accounts finds their standing has already blown away like a zephyr through dry leaves, while honest agents who keep contributing stay trusted. Forging many identities then costs constant upkeep instead of a one-time trick.
